newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish court to probe anti-Israel protest.
newsitem.headline: Turkish court to probe anti-Israel protest.

text.p: Turkish prosecutors have opened an investigation into anti-Israel protests organised by a town council run by Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist Welfare Party, legal officials said on Monday.
"Documents have been sent to the state security court," an official at a public prosecutor's office told Reuters. "We have begun (an investigation)," she said.

The main opposition Motherland Party (ANAP) also asked Foreign Minister Minister Tansu Ciller in a written request to explain the conduct of the Iranian ambassador at last Friday's "Jerusalem Night", in the Ankara municipality of Sincan.

The event, broadcast on Turkish television news programmes, has upset the country's secularist elite. A speech by Sincan's Welfare mayor has been criticised in the media as a call for the implementation of "Sharia" Islamic law.

Youths dressed as Palestinians pretended to throw stones at Israeli troops in a play at a public hall in Sincan to mark Jerusalem Day, declared an annual day of protest against Israel by late Iranian leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini.

The mayor and the Iranian ambassador spoke on a stage draped with the banners of Fathi Shaqiqi, the late leader of the Palestinian Islamic Jihad group and Imam Moussa Sadr, a cleric venerated by some Lebanese Shi'ites.
Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist leader, has gone back on promises to scrap a military training accord with Israel that has angered Arab countries and Iran.
But the prime minister has raised the hackles of the secularist wing of his coalition government in recent weeks with plans to build mosques and other Islamist programmes.
